open_questions: Mass measurement needed to rule out brown dwarf given size near detection limit
High impact parameter (b ~0.1023 fit, duration ratio 1.463) should be checked with higher-precision follow-up
Off-target / neighbour blend not localized (centroid inconclusive, 1 plausible neighbour within 1 px) - centroid on a brightened aperture must be confirmed
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 14.2-day, 600 ppm transit with no secondary eclipse or odd-even change, consistent with ~2 Earth-radius planet. The apparent sector depth scatter is calibration between instruments and individual transits are steady apart from one undetected transit. A V shape, stellar eclipse or blended EB is not supported, so a small planet on the target is the best explanation despite an unresolved centroid.

reasons.why: Super-Earth-sized transit, far below stellar eclipse range, favours planet over EB even without flat-bottom check alone
Not V-shaped (negative v_sigma) supports non-grazing planetary transit morphology
No significant secondary eclipse (snr 2.37 vs best_brightening_snr 2.965) and no phase curve (amplitude 116 ppm ratio_to_depth 0.1959) argues against stellar companion
Odd/even depth difference not significant; no indication of binary at twice period (28.4 d)
No difference image to locate dip, but neighbours.plausible_within_1px = 1 does not outweigh planet evidence and depth is too small for typical blend to be confident off-target

Apparent depth change (sectors p_constant 4.726e-7) is calibration between QLP (612 ppm), SPOC 2-min (578/1069 ppm) and TESS-SPOC (-29 ppm); within SPOC 2-min p_constant 0.017134719910159486 shows steady signal, transit_depths outliers explained by TESS-SPOC non-detection to deep QLP detection
Duration ratio 1.463 is long (5 h vs central 3.418 h) but stellar parameters consistent between TIC and Gaia, implying high impact parameter/eccentricity rather than evolved star or mis-modelling
